exposure.note: Ready = a canary plinth complete AND a _well_built at its cap in a window >= 180 min (unchanged definition). Caps come from the canary's _plinth rows AND the canary pools' plinth records, so the plinths finished under plinth-01 (board-c 365,73,137; hive-d 56,64,69) count when a canary bot builds their well.

own_lines.note: P1: a canary _plinth_step placement outside the 81-cell shell of its cap or a stair line. Self-tests in the read on the bot's row strings.
P2: a build visit that placed and left the bag under 64 reserve stone (the exit contract's reserve).
P3: a plinth column walled in and uncovered > 10 min (the last pit event at the cap dug/open). wellread C9 judges the same rows per pool.
P4: a raised well retired (breached) -- the plinth did not hold.
P5: two or more canary entombment / stranded / livelock rows within 3 of a plinth cap. One is named, not a verdict.
Leak: a CONTROL _plinth row means the control is not running the base. Blocks KEEP (no evidence key).
junkwell-02 C1, at a raised well.
junkwell-02 C5: throws from the raised stand.
junkwell-02 C9: the plinth's pit rows (_well_pit_dug from=plinth*, _well_pit_covered stage=plinth) are the well's own kinds, judged per pool and site.

primary.note: REPORTED, NOT GATED: dispose_well successes per bot-h, canary vs control towns WITHOUT a well, pre vs post (DiD); planned/complete towns, blocks placed, alt stands, step pace. WATCH (Claude rebase P3-1): orderroom room remedies via=well toward a plinth site recorded but not yet capped (a walk home that finds no usable well; bounded 1 per bot per 30 min). MECHANISM (report only): build refusals for want of a table cell per bot-h, canary vs control, pre vs post (plinth-01's window: canary 0.000 -> 0.767, control 0 -> 0).

harm.note: Unchanged: the two-death floor (OWNER 2026-09-11) and gather_ratio < 0.43 of control, from immobiledid. A death within 3 of a plinth is named, never a verdict.

teardown.note: THREE STEPS: drop-ins, clear canary_pool, restart the pool's bots 12 s apart; then confirm the live versions. A plinth stays in the world after a REVERT: a block of cobble whose open column (if any) its builder covered; the base never reads the plinth record; a covered or capped column is inert. A crafting table build_well put down beside or on a plinth stays (inert town furniture).
